# lmux

> lmux is a light, native macOS terminal for running Claude Code and Codex CLI all day. It's a 25 MB app
> built on libghostty (Ghostty's terminal core) with a sidebar of workspaces, splits in any direction, and
> agent status in the sidebar, so you can see which of many Claude Code or Codex sessions is working, done
> or waiting for you. It's free, MIT licensed, and makes no network calls. A lightweight alternative to cmux.

Key facts:

- What it is: a terminal emulator app for macOS, written in Swift (AppKit) on libghostty. Not a wrapper: it
  never wraps `claude` or `codex`, it listens to Claude Code's hooks and to the state Codex reports itself.
- Platforms: macOS 14 (Sonoma) or later, Apple silicon only. No Linux or Windows version.
- License: MIT. Author: Soohwan Kim ([sooftware](https://github.com/sooftware)). Source: https://github.com/sooftware/lmux
- Install: `brew install --cask sooftware/tap/lmux`, or download the app from https://github.com/sooftware/lmux/releases/latest
- Agent features: per-session status (running, needs you, done, failed) with a jump to the one waiting
  (`⇧⌘J`), rewinding a turn and undo send (Claude Code only), History search across past sessions, and every
  Claude Code and Codex session resumed after a quit, update or reboot. Any other CLI runs as in any terminal.
- vs cmux: same sidebar-and-splits idea with a smaller scope, written from scratch (not a fork, no cmux code).
  lmux leaves out cmux's browser panes, SSH workspaces, custom commands, command palette and sidebar widgets,
  and has about 10 settings instead of about 200. Measured on an M4 Pro with 20 idle workspaces: 25 MB app vs
  242 MB, 235 MB memory vs 661 MB, 0.10% idle CPU vs 8.10% (lmux 0.0.102 vs cmux 0.65.2, method in
  scripts/BENCH.md). It can import a cmux setup (theme, fonts, shortcuts, open workspaces) in one click, with
  Undo Import.
- vs Ghostty: lmux reads your Ghostty config as is and adds the agent-aware sidebar, rewind and resume.
- vs tmux: workspaces and splits replace tmux sessions and panes, with Mac shortcuts and no prefix key. There's
  no server, so running processes don't survive a quit; Claude Code and Codex sessions resume instead.
- Korean input: fixes upstream Ghostty's Hangul IME problems (Enter, Backspace, Esc and shortcuts
  mid-syllable), and `⌃C` reaches Claude Code as Ctrl+C with the Korean input source on.

- [Agent guide](https://lmux.dev/agent-guide.md): everything an agent needs to set lmux up for someone, in one Markdown file
- [Full docs as plain text](https://lmux.dev/llms-full.txt): every docs page below in one file

## Docs

- [Install](https://lmux.dev/docs/install/): lmux, a light terminal for Claude Code and Codex, runs on macOS 14 (Sonoma) or later, on Apple silicon. It's one app, with the lmux command line tool inside it.
- [Quick start](https://lmux.dev/docs/quick-start/): lmux is a light macOS terminal for Claude Code and Codex. Its first launch takes a minute: two offers, each with one button, and then it's a terminal.
- [Workspaces & panes](https://lmux.dev/docs/workspaces/): lmux, a macOS terminal for Claude Code and Codex, has one window, a sidebar of workspaces, and splits inside each one. A workspace is what a window is in…
- [Shortcuts](https://lmux.dev/docs/shortcuts/): lmux is a macOS terminal on libghostty, and these are its default shortcuts. A keybind in your Ghostty config wins over them, and the menus always show…
- [Configuration](https://lmux.dev/docs/configuration/): lmux is a macOS terminal on libghostty, and it's configured the way Ghostty is: one plain-text file in Ghostty's syntax. It reads your Ghostty config as it…
- [Korean input](https://lmux.dev/docs/korean-input/): What lmux fixes for Korean input: Enter, Backspace, Esc and shortcuts mid-syllable, and Hangul at exactly two cells in D2Coding.
- [한글 입력 (한국어)](https://lmux.dev/docs/ko/): Claude Code와 Codex에 한글로 작업을 시킬 때 터미널 IME에서 생기는 문제, lmux에서 고친 내용, 테스트 방법을 정리했습니다.
- [Claude Code](https://lmux.dev/docs/claude-code/): lmux is a light macOS terminal built for living in Claude Code. It shows which session needs you, lets you take back a turn, and brings every session back…
- [Codex](https://lmux.dev/docs/codex/): Codex CLI gets most of what Claude Code gets in lmux, a light macOS terminal on libghostty, by listening only: status, notifications, resume on restart,…
- [Any agent (OSC 7501)](https://lmux.dev/docs/any-agent/): Any CLI runs in lmux, a light macOS terminal on libghostty. Status, rewind, resume and History are built for Claude Code and Codex. This page is about the…
- [The lmux CLI](https://lmux.dev/docs/cli/): lmux, a macOS terminal for Claude Code and Codex, ships a small command line tool, lmux, for scripts and agents. It's on the PATH in every lmux pane; the…
- [lmux vs cmux](https://lmux.dev/docs/vs-cmux/): lmux is a lightweight alternative to cmux: the same sidebar and splits, built on libghostty, in a 25 MB app with about ten settings. Here's when to pick which.
- [Switching from cmux](https://lmux.dev/docs/from-cmux/): lmux is a lightweight alternative to cmux that borrows its layout, so the sidebar and splits work the way you're used to. Moving over should feel like…
- [Performance](https://lmux.dev/docs/performance/): lmux's one rule is to stay light. It's a 25 MB native macOS terminal that idles near 0% CPU, whether you have one workspace open or twenty.
- [Privacy & files on disk](https://lmux.dev/docs/privacy/): lmux, a macOS terminal for Claude Code and Codex, makes no network calls at all: no telemetry, no crash reports, not even an update check (Homebrew does…
- [Troubleshooting](https://lmux.dev/docs/troubleshooting/): Fixes for the few things that go wrong: Claude's dark prompt band, a sidebar that never updates, Codex hooks, macOS permission prompts, CLI errors.
- [FAQ](https://lmux.dev/docs/faq/): Is lmux a cmux alternative, why not Ghostty and tmux, does it work with Codex or without Claude Code, does it phone home, and more.
